item.title: I spent hours with my brand designer last week. 💙
item.description:
I spent hours with my brand designer last week. 💙
Not on logos. Not on colours. On my why.
We went back to the beginning… the Loves that run through every business I've built. The thread that ties all of it together. I sat there and watched my whole journey laid out in front of me, and I came away from those hours feeling more reconnected to the heart of JLT than I had in months. Maybe years.
But here is what caught me off guard.
The whole afternoon was a quiet reminder that heart needs something underneath it. I lead with heart in everything I do. It is the reason JLT exists at all. It is in every decision I make, every agent I bring in, every late reply I send because I cannot leave someone waiting. Yet heart on its own, with nothing to hold it up, is exhausting.
I learned that the slow way.
For years I thought passion was the engine. That if I cared enough, worked hard enough, loved the work enough, the rest would somehow follow. And it did carry me a long way. But it also wore me thin. Caring deeply with no boundaries around it meant I said yes to everything and everyone. I poured out and out and never paused to ask what was sustainable. There were evenings I gave away that I will never get back. There were moments my family got the tired version of me, because I had spent all the good hours on the business and kept nothing in reserve.
The lesson took me far too long to learn… the processes are not the enemy of heart. They protect it.
Boundaries are not cold. The back-end of a business is not corporate. The structure around what you do is the thing that lets the heart keep beating without burning out. When I finally built real boundaries into how I work… set hours, clear limits, a back-end I could trust… I found I had more to give, not less. The discipline freed up the passion. The structure gave the heart room to breathe.
If you are a heart-led agent, I think you already know the feeling I mean. You love your clients. You want to do right by every single one of them. And some weeks that love leaves you running on empty, because there is nothing underneath it holding the weight.
Here is the gentle permission I wish someone had handed me years ago.
You can care deeply and still have boundaries. You can lead with heart and still build the processes that protect your time, your energy, your evenings. The two are not in conflict. One keeps the other alive.
Heart is why we start. Structure is how we keep going.
So if you have been telling yourself that being organised somehow makes you less passionate, less warm, less you… let that one go. The back-end is not the opposite of heart. It is the thing that guards it, so the heart can do what it does best.
Keep showing up. The warm way and the wise way, both at once. 🌱
Janine x

item.title: Looking back on everything I've built, the thing I'm proudest of isn't the number of agents, or the bookings, or any milestone I could point to on a slide. 💙
item.description:
Looking back on everything I've built, the thing I'm proudest of isn't the number of agents, or the bookings, or any milestone I could point to on a slide. 💙
It's that I can stand behind how I got here.
I can look at every decision and know I made it with my heart in the right place. That matters more to me now than it did when I started.
When I was younger in business, I thought success was a scoreboard. Bigger numbers. More noise. A harder edge. I believed you had to be a certain type of person to be taken seriously… a bit cooler, a bit tougher, less soft.
So for a while I tried to be that person.
And it never sat right. I'd come away from those moments feeling like I'd borrowed someone else's voice. Like I was playing a part instead of building something real.
The change came slowly, over time. I noticed the moments I felt most proud were never the ruthless ones. They were the kind ones. The agent I took an extra hour with. The honest answer I gave when an easier one was right there. The fairness I chose when nobody would have known the difference.
Those moments cost me sometimes. A bit of margin. A bit of speed. But they're the ones I can look back on without flinching.
That's when it clicked for me. Kindness was never the weak option. It was the harder one. Anyone can cut a corner. Standing by your values when it would be easier not to… that takes real backbone.
The wins matter, of course they do. But the wins fade. What stays is whether you can look at how you got them and feel at peace.
If you're building something right now, I want you to hear this. You don't have to harden up to be successful. You don't have to become someone you don't recognise. The people who last are rarely the loudest or the most ruthless. They're the ones who built on something solid… something they can stand behind. 🌱
So when you're faced with the choice between the quick way and the right way, and no one's watching, choose the one you'll be proud of later. That choice IS your legacy. Not the number. The way you got to it.
You can be kind and still be strong. You can be gentle and still be taken seriously. In fact, I think that's the only real success worth having.
Build something you can stand behind. Then you never have to look over your shoulder.
Keep going. You're building something good.
Janine x

item.title: One thing I've learned leading a team over the years is that most of the job lives in a narrow gap. Not the big speeches. Not the tough calls everyone remembers. The gap between being too soft and being too sharp… that's where the real work sits. And I'm still figuring it out, most weeks. 💙
item.description:
One thing I've learned leading a team over the years is that most of the job lives in a narrow gap. Not the big speeches. Not the tough calls everyone remembers. The gap between being too soft and being too sharp… that's where the real work sits. And I'm still figuring it out, most weeks. 💙
For a long time I thought there was a setting you arrived at. A version of yourself you switched on for work. Firm. Decisive. The leader people picture when they say the word. So I tried to be that. And it never sat right on me.
Then I overcorrected the other way. Warm with everyone, all the time, smoothing every edge so nobody felt a knock. That didn't sit right either. Because being endlessly soft isn't kindness. Sometimes it's me avoiding the harder conversation because I want to be liked more than I want to be useful.
Here is what I notice now. The calibration isn't a one-time decision. It's daily. Hourly, some days. The same words that come across as care for one person on a Monday can feel like pressure to another by Friday. You read the room. You read the person. You adjust. You get it slightly wrong, and you adjust again.
The thing nobody tells you is that kind and firm are not opposites. I used to hold them as a dial, where more of one meant less of the other. They're not. The kindest thing I do some days is be clear. Telling someone the truth about their work, gently and without dressing it up, is warmer than letting them carry on into a wall. Soft on the person. Honest about the thing. That's the line I keep coming back to.
And it costs me something to find it, every time. There's a small fear in the firm direction… that I'll be seen as cold, that someone will think I've changed. And a different fear in the soft direction… that I'm not being honest enough to help. Sitting between the two is uncomfortable. I've made peace with the fact that it's meant to be.
If you're leading anyone, mentoring a newer agent, building a little team around you, you'll know this gap. You'll have days where you replay a conversation and wonder if you were too blunt. And days you wonder if you let something slide you shouldn't have. 🌱
I want to hand you the permission I had to grow into. You don't have to fit the mould of the hard, no-nonsense leader to be taken seriously. That mould was never the only way. Kindness is not the soft option. Holding warmth and honesty in the same hand is harder than picking one and hiding behind it.
The leaders I trust most aren't the sharpest in the room. They're the ones who can be honest with me without making me feel small. That's not weakness. That's the most skilled thing a person can do with their words, and it takes years to get even close.
So if you're recalibrating this week, getting it slightly wrong, adjusting, getting it slightly wrong again… you're not failing at leadership. You're doing the actual work of it. The calibration never finishes. The good ones keep paying attention.
You won't find the perfect setting. There isn't one. There's only you, reading the moment, and choosing warmth and honesty together, one conversation at a time.
Keep showing up for your people. They feel the care more than you think.
Janine x
